source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's DFW2 campus in Lewisville publishes 12 MW of IT capacity across 200,000 square feet, and that is the only power figure the operator discloses.

The published number is a ceiling on what the building can deliver to IT equipment, not a measure of what is installed. No rack count, accelerator count, or power usage effectiveness is stated, so any conversion to racks or GPUs depends on an assumed density. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 12 MW is roughly 300 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is roughly 1,200. The arithmetic is an assumption about density, not a fact about this building.

The certifications qualify the campus for specific workloads rather than describing who occupies it. PCI DSS covers payment card data, HIPAA covers protected health information, ISO 27001 covers an information security management system, FISMA covers federal information systems, SSAE 16 Type II covers controls relevant to financial reporting, and TIA-942 covers telecommunications infrastructure design. None names a tenant.

Texas holds 137 mapped facilities, of which 19 publish a megawatt figure. Those 19 total 475.41 MW, and DFW2 ranks twelfth among them. The ranking sits within a minority of Texas facilities, since most mapped sites publish no figure at all. On the published numbers this is a mid-sized campus in the largest concentration of data centers mapped here, and its 12 MW is a small share of the state's published total. What the data does not cover is whether the campus is expanding, what tenants it holds, or how much of its published capacity is energized today.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
